name: Burlington Stores, Inc.

events.what: Independent director added (routine refresh, not a catalyst)
EVP and Chief Human Resources Officer departed

Burlington 2.0 long-range plan (2023 to 2028) set two years before 2025-11-25, i.e. about 2023; CEO Michael O'Sullivan unchanged; no CEO or CFO change and no Item 2.01/1.01 deal found since 2024-07-01

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Management frames adjusted EBIT margin as ~400 bps of expansion between 2023 and 2028 plus ~$1.6B operating income by 2028 (company fiscal 2028 = Baba FY-2029, FYE January). No explicit level was found; target_level_pct is DERIVED on the consensus operating_income basis: FY2025 consensus-basis margin 7.67% (887.1M / 11,566.9M) plus the 220 bps still to go after 100 bps (2024) and 80 bps (2025). Company adjusted EBIT ($923M per DEF 14A) runs about 30 bps above the consensus operating_income line.

statements.quote: As a reminder, our long-range model calls for approximately 400 basis points of operating margin expansion between 2023 and 2028.
statements.speaker: Michael O'Sullivan
statements.doc_title: BURLINGTON STORES INC Q4 2025 Earnings Call

statements.quote: So two years ago, we shared our objective of getting to approximately $1.6 billion in operating income by 2028. The headline is that we feel very good about the progress we're making toward this goal.
statements.speaker: Kristin Wolfe
statements.doc_title: BURLINGTON STORES INC Q3 2026 Earnings Call (company Q3 fiscal 2025)

statements.quote: At the high end of our updated 2025 margin guidance, we will have achieved 170 basis points of the 400 basis points of opportunity that we identified two years ago.
statements.speaker: Kristin Wolfe
statements.doc_title: BURLINGTON STORES INC Q3 2026 Earnings Call (company Q3 fiscal 2025)

statements.quote: We achieved 80 basis points of operating margin expansion on top of 100 basis points last year and 22% earnings per share growth on top of 34% last year.
statements.speaker: Michael O'Sullivan
statements.doc_title: BURLINGTON STORES INC Q4 2026 Earnings Call (company Q4 fiscal 2025)

statements.quote: We expect comp store sales to increase in the range of 3%-4%, and our adjusted EBIT margin to expand by 20 basis points to 40 basis points versus last year.
statements.speaker: Kristin Wolfe
statements.doc_title: BURLINGTON STORES INC Q2 2027 Earnings Call (company Q2 fiscal 2026)

street.gap_assumption: Baba FY labels (FY2026 = company fiscal 2025, reported). Gap compares the derived 9.87% operating margin for company fiscal 2028 with consensus Baba FY-2029 operating_income / revenue (1,384.6M / 15,202.4M = 9.11%), same basis. In dollars, $1.6B target vs $1,384.6M consensus = +15.6%, partly a sales gap (comp plan of 4% to 5% a year vs 3% to 4% now guided).

evidence_of_progress.note: Order is [Q1 fiscal 2026 (May-2026), Q2 fiscal 2026 (Aug-2026)], company-stated adjusted EBIT margin YoY (Q1 6.3%, +20 bps; Q2 7.0%, +100 bps excl. $55M tariff refunds, Wolfe doc 199910). Q1 EBITDA margin from consensus actuals +16 bps. Q3 fiscal 2026 guided down 60 to 80 bps as refunds are reinvested; full-year guide +20 to 40 bps.

disqualifier_reason: No catalyst in the 18-month window and none pending: CEO O'Sullivan and CFO Wolfe unchanged, no acquisition, and the Burlington 2.0 framework dates from about 2023. The margin story is also largely underwritten already: consensus sits only about 76 bps short of the implied 2028 margin, with 12-month EBITDA revisions +6.8%.
verdict: Not a GXO setup: a dated, repeated 400 bps / $1.6B 2028 framework that management is executing on, but there is no new-management catalyst and the street already models most of it (about 76 bps short on margin), so the gap is small and the stock is not low-margin versus peers.
open_questions: Will management restate or raise the $1.6B 2028 operating income goal now that comps run 3% to 4% against the 4% to 5% plan?
How much of the 2026 margin beat is tariff relief (merch margin +70 bps) that reverses as refunds are reinvested in Q3 and Q4?
Does the street's 9.1% fiscal 2028 margin already assume the full supply chain productivity bucket (about 100 of the 400 bps)?
